report_md:
# Beta rotation — development report

**Verdict: dev pass.** The QQQ-vs-SPY beta state earns **42.96% CAGR / 47.72%
max DD / 1.15 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023, above the published TQQQ bar
(36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82) with a much lower drawdown. The result survives 5 bp
(41.88%) and 10 bp (40.55%) and the circular-shift placebo (real CAGR is at the
100th percentile of 100 timing-scrambled paths). It is a development-only
result; 2024-2026 is untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 42.96% | 47.72% | 1.15 | 1.65 | 37.3% | 99.9% | 151 | 732x |
| 5 bp | 41.88% | 47.80% | 1.13 | 1.62 | 37.3% | 99.9% | 151 | 702x |
| 10 bp | 40.55% | 48.22% | 1.10 | 1.59 | 37.3% | 99.9% | 151 | 666x |

There are **151 fills across 76 independent fill days** (the activity floor is
100 fills or 30 events). Average weights are 69.0% QQQ, 27.9% TQQQ, 3.1% BIL.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 27.3% | 30.6% | 1.12 |
| 2020-2021 | 116.8% | 33.9% | 1.34 |
| 2022-2023 | 17.4% | 47.0% | 0.59 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +20.0% |
| 2017 | +49.1% |
| 2018 | -1.8% |
| 2019 | +44.9% |
| 2020 | +174.0% |
| 2021 | +78.3% |
| 2022 | -39.4% |
| 2023 | +131.9% |

The 2022 loss is the main weakness: beta expansion is a slow risk signal, so
the strategy gives back a large part of the bear market before the BIL state
takes over. The 2023 recovery and the 2020-2021 trend do the heavy lifting.

## Plateau (pre-registered 2 x 2 x 2)

| Beta | pct_tqqq | asym_tqqq | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| blend 42/63 | 0.50 | 0.00 | 37.41% | 47.4% | 1.08 | 139 |
| **blend 42/63** | **0.60** | **0.00** | **42.96%** | **47.7%** | **1.15** | **151** |
| blend 42/63 | 0.50 | 0.05 | 42.79% | 51.0% | 1.10 | 151 |
| blend 42/63 | 0.60 | 0.05 | 49.81% | 54.6% | 1.12 | 135 |
| single 63 | 0.50 | 0.00 | 30.56% | 57.9% | 0.92 | 143 |
| single 63 | 0.60 | 0.00 | 39.15% | 52.9% | 1.05 | 139 |
| single 63 | 0.50 | 0.05 | 32.42% | 63.4% | 0.90 | 127 |
| single 63 | 0.60 | 0.05 | 43.24% | 58.8% | 1.01 | 101 |

Six of eight cells clear the published CAGR bar. The two single-63 low-
compression cells (0.50) do not, which is the honest soft spot: the fast 42-day
beta matters. The headline uses the 42/63 blend at the centre of the grid, not
the best cell (the best cell is 49.81% at asym 0.05).

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 21.2%, 95th percentile
  35.8%; the real 42.96% is above all 100 shifts (percentile 1.00). Median
  placebo Sharpe 0.69 vs the real 1.15.
* **Static book at the average weights (69.0/27.9/3.1):** 25.33% CAGR / 53.5%
  DD / 0.85 Sharpe. The timing adds 17.6 percentage points of CAGR and 0.30
  Sharpe, so the beta state is not just a disguised fixed mix.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

Range **0.52 to 0.78**. Highest: `family-rebalance-flow` 0.78,
`relative-value-tqqq` 0.76; lowest: `family-intraday-microstructure-day` 0.52,
`ratio-froth` 0.57. No correlation approaches the 0.95 duplicate threshold.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 42.96% | yes |
| 1 bp DD < 82.29% | 47.72% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 40.55% | yes |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 100% | yes |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.78 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 151 / 76 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | all positive | yes |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 25.33% vs 42.96% | yes |

## Caveats

* Beta uses local SPY daily closes, not the QQQ/TQQQ/BIL 1-minute panel. The
  regressor is daily by construction; the traded panel remains the shared
  1-minute data.
* The 42-day beta is the fast end of the grid. The 63-day-only result is
  39.15%, still a pass, but the gap is a real sensitivity.
* 2022 is -39.4%. This is a risk-on/risk-off family, not a crash-proof one.
* The 2016 partial year uses the QQQ fallback while the 252-day percentile
  warms up; it is not a full TQQQ year.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-beta-rotation
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` accepts the shared minute panel or a daily
panel; the lead's `run_holdout.py` can call it directly.
hypothesis_md:
# family-beta-rotation — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-beta-rotation`
**Family:** beta rotation
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not loaded
or inspected by the development run.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 35.81% / 82.30% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

TQQQ is a constant 3x wrapper on QQQ, but QQQ's sensitivity to the equity
market is not constant. The rolling QQQ-vs-SPY beta measures how much of QQQ's
move is broad-market beta rather than a Nasdaq-specific trend:

* **Beta compression** (beta low in its own one-year range) means QQQ is moving
  on a low-stress, relatively idiosyncratic trend. A 3x daily-reset wrapper
  compounds well when the underlying path is smooth and the market factor is
  not dominating: there are fewer high-correlation gap-down days and the 3x
  reset is paid for by the trend rather than by two-sided variance.
* **Beta expansion** means the market factor is taking over. In that state QQQ
  and TQQQ drawdowns become market-wide and correlated; the 3x wrapper is
  dangerous even if the Nasdaq trend still looks intact.
* **Upside/downside beta asymmetry** separates a healthy high-beta tape from a
  stressed one. `beta_up - beta_down` is high when QQQ captures more of SPY's
  up moves than its down moves. Very high asymmetry is not a buy signal: the
  leverage has already been paid for, and forward TQQQ returns are weaker.

The primary object is the beta vector (level percentile plus up/down
asymmetry), not relative-strength momentum, a moving-average trend gate, or a
volatility target.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use daily closes through session `t`. The target is set at the close
of `t` and executed at the first bar open of `t+1` (the shared 2% band applies).

Let `r_Q` and `r_S` be daily log returns of QQQ and SPY.

1. `beta_42` and `beta_63` are rolling OLS betas of `r_Q` on `r_S` over 42 and
   63 sessions. `beta = (beta_42 + beta_63) / 2`.
2. `pct` is the fraction of the prior **252** `beta` observations (excluding
   the current one) that are below today's `beta`. Missing warm-up values
   default to 0.5.
3. `beta_up` / `beta_down` are OLS betas over the prior **126** sessions using
   only SPY-up days and only SPY-down days. `asym = beta_up - beta_down`.
4. State:
   * **TQQQ** if `pct < 0.60` **and** `asym < 0.00`;
   * **QQQ** if `pct < 0.80` **or** `asym < 0.15` (and the TQQQ condition did
     not fire);
   * **BIL** otherwise.

The state is held through the next session. Weights are long-only, sum to 1,
and are fractions of equity.

## 3. Estimation window and decision clock

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Beta windows | 42 and 63 sessions, averaged |
| Beta percentile window | 252 sessions, current observation excluded |
| Up/down beta window | 126 sessions |
| Data | local adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py`; local SPY daily adjusted closes for the beta regressor |
| Decision | close of session `t` |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |

SPY is read from `data/round3/yahoo/SPY-1d-yahoo.parquet` and filtered to the
requested panel's last date before any use. During the development run that
drops every 2024-2026 row before it is inspected.

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not `ratio-froth` / `relative-value-tqqq`: there is no TQQQ/QQQ ratio, no
  ratio momentum and no QQQ moving-average trend gate.
* Not `qqq-spy-relative`: that family uses relative strength of QQQ versus SPY.
  Here the object is the *covariance* (beta) and its up/down asymmetry; the
  strategy never ranks QQQ and SPY returns against each other.
* Not a volatility target: no position is sized by `target_vol / realised_vol`.
  The state is driven by the beta percentile and the asymmetry sign.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

The grid is 2 x 2 x 2: beta estimate (blend 42/63 vs single 63), compression
threshold (0.50 vs 0.60), asymmetry threshold (0.00 vs 0.05). Fixed:
`pct_qqq = 0.80`, `asym_qqq = 0.15`.

The primary cell is the blend with `pct_tqqq = 0.60` and `asym_tqqq = 0.00`.
It is the centre of the mechanism, not the best cell in the grid.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

The family is killed if any of the following holds on the development window:

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max DD >= 82.29% (the published TQQQ bar).
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% (the edge is a cost artefact).
3. The circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile is below 90%.
4. Daily-return correlation with any current family winner is above 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any of the three subperiods (2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023) has a
   negative CAGR.
7. A static book at the strategy's average weights matches the 1 bp CAGR
   within 1 percentage point (then the timing adds nothing).

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 38-45% |
| max DD | 45-55% |
| Sharpe | 1.0-1.2 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.25-0.35 |
| correlation to winners | 0.55-0.80 |

If the result is in these ranges with a positive placebo and a materially
worse static blend, the beta object carries information. The report states the
2022 loss and the fast-beta sensitivity plainly.

code:
"""family-beta-rotation -- QQQ-vs-SPY beta compression/expansion rotation.

Primary object: the rolling beta of QQQ to SPY, not relative-strength momentum.
The strategy holds TQQQ only when beta is compressed in its own recent history
and downside beta does not dominate upside beta; otherwise QQQ, and BIL when
beta is in the top of its one-year range and asymmetry is unfavourable.

Decision clock: a target is set from the close of session t (all inputs use
returns through that close) and executed at the next session's first bar open.
The backtester's 2% band and next-open fill rule are unchanged.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# run_holdout.py loads this file by path without adding its directory to
# sys.path; make the local harness importable in both entry points.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import harness

SLUG = "family-beta-rotation"
FAMILY = "beta-rotation"
PRIMARY = "rolling QQQ-vs-SPY beta (level percentile and up/down asymmetry)"

PARAMS = {
    "beta_windows": (42, 63),
    "pct_lookback": 252,
    "pct_tqqq": 0.60,
    "pct_qqq": 0.80,
    "asym_window": 126,
    "asym_tqqq": 0.00,
    "asym_qqq": 0.15,
}

# 2 x 2 x 2 pre-registered grid: beta estimate, compression threshold,
# asymmetry threshold.  The primary cell is (blend, 0.60, 0.00).
PLATEAU = [
    {"beta_windows": (42, 63), "pct_tqqq": 0.50, "asym_tqqq": 0.00},
    {"beta_windows": (42, 63), "pct_tqqq": 0.60, "asym_tqqq": 0.00},
    {"beta_windows": (42, 63), "pct_tqqq": 0.50, "asym_tqqq": 0.05},
    {"beta_windows": (42, 63), "pct_tqqq": 0.60, "asym_tqqq": 0.05},
    {"beta_windows": (63,), "pct_tqqq": 0.50, "asym_tqqq": 0.00},
    {"beta_windows": (63,), "pct_tqqq": 0.60, "asym_tqqq": 0.00},
    {"beta_windows": (63,), "pct_tqqq": 0.50, "asym_tqqq": 0.05},
    {"beta_windows": (63,), "pct_tqqq": 0.60, "asym_tqqq": 0.05},
]


def _rolling_beta(rq: np.ndarray, rs: np.ndarray, win: int, nd: int) -> np.ndarray:
    out = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    for i in range(win, nd):
        x = rs[i - win:i]
        y = rq[i - win:i]
        vx = float(x.var())
        if vx > 0:
            out[i] = float(np.cov(y, x, ddof=0)[0, 1]) / vx
    return out


def _pct_rank(beta: np.ndarray, lookback: int) -> np.ndarray:
    nd = len(beta)
    pct = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    for i in range(lookback, nd):
        hist = beta[i - lookback:i]
        hist = hist[np.isfinite(hist)]
        if len(hist) > 100:
            pct[i] = float((hist < beta[i]).mean())
    return np.nan_to_num(pct, nan=0.5)


def _updown_beta(rq: np.ndarray, rs: np.ndarray, win: int, nd: int):
    bu = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    bd = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    for i in range(win, nd):
        y = rq[i - win:i]
        x = rs[i - win:i]
        up = x > 0
        dn = x < 0
        if int(up.sum()) > 5 and float(x[up].var()) > 0:
            bu[i] = float(np.cov(y[up], x[up], ddof=0)[0, 1]) / float(x[up].var())
        if int(dn.sum()) > 5 and float(x[dn].var()) > 0:
            bd[i] = float(np.cov(y[dn], x[dn], ddof=0)[0, 1]) / float(x[dn].var())
    return bu, bd


def make_targets(dates, closes: np.ndarray, spy: pd.Series,
                 params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    nd = len(dates)
    rq = np.diff(np.log(closes[:, 0]))
    rs = np.diff(np.log(spy.to_numpy(dtype=float)))
    betas = [_rolling_beta(rq, rs, int(w), nd) for w in p["beta_windows"]]
    stack = np.vstack(betas)
    cnt = np.isfinite(stack).sum(axis=0)
    beta = np.nansum(stack, axis=0) / np.maximum(cnt, 1)
    beta[cnt == 0] = np.nan
    pct = _pct_rank(beta, int(p["pct_lookback"]))
    bu, bd = _updown_beta(rq, rs, int(p["asym_window"]), nd)
    asym = np.nan_to_num(bu - bd, nan=0.0)

    w = np.zeros((nd, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0                       # BIL by default
    qqq = (pct < p["pct_qqq"]) | (asym < p["asym_qqq"])
    w[qqq] = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    tqqq = (pct < p["pct_tqqq"]) & (asym < p["asym_tqqq"])
    w[tqqq] = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    spy = harness.load_spy(dates)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes, spy, params)
    if len(ts) == len(dates):
        return daily          # daily panel: caller applies the next-open shift
    return harness.expand(ts, daily)


def _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes, spy) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for cell in PLATEAU:
        w = harness.expand(ts, make_targets(dates, closes, spy, cell))
        st = harness.metrics(harness.simulate(ts, o, c, w, bp=1.0))
        out.append({
            "cell": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                     for k, v in cell.items()},
            "cagr": st["cagr"], "max_drawdown": st["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": st["sharpe"], "fills": st["fills"],
            "turnover": st["turnover"],
        })
    return out


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = harness.load_panel()
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    spy = harness.load_spy(dates)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes, spy)
    ev = harness.evaluate(ts, o, c, daily, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    max_corr = max(ev["corr_winners"].values())
    kills = {
        "cagr_below_published_tqqq_bar": st["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "drawdown_above_tqqq": st["max_drawdown"] >= 0.8229,
        "cost_10bp_below_bar": ev["stats"]["10bp"]["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "placebo_below_90pct": ev["placebo"]["cagr_percentile_of_real"] < 0.90,
        "correlation_above_0.95": max_corr > 0.95,
        "fewer_than_100_fills": st["fills"] < 100,
        "fewer_than_30_events": ev["events"] < 30,
        "negative_subperiod": any(v["cagr"] < 0 for v in ev["subperiods"].values()),
        "static_blend_matches": (ev["static_avg_weights"]["cagr"] >= st["cagr"] - 0.01),
    }
    verdict = "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail"
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG, "family": FAMILY, "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [harness.START, harness.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": {"cagr": 0.3581, "max_drawdown": 0.823, "sharpe": 0.80},
            "tqqq_published_bar": {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229,
                                   "sharpe": 0.82},
        },
        "params": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                   for k, v in PARAMS.items()},
        "stats": ev["stats"], "events": ev["events"],
        "yearly": ev["yearly"], "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes, spy),
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "kill_checks": kills, "verdict": verdict,
        "timing": ("Signal uses daily closes through session t; target executed "
                   "at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band; long only."),
        "notes": ("Beta uses local SPY daily adjusted closes, filtered to the "
                  "requested panel end before use. No 2024-2026 rows are read "
                  "during the development run."),
    }
    harness.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {harness.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", harness.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", verdict)
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
